predecessors.name: Banate of Bosnia
predecessors.text: the Banate of Bosnia, raised to a kingdom when Tvrtko I was crowned in the fall of 1377 (probably 26 October)

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the kingdom's heartland, conquered by Mehmed II in May 1463 and organised as the Sanjak of Bosnia (Isa-beg first sanjakbey in 1464)

successors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
successors.text: Jajce and its fortress, retaken by Matthias on 26 December 1463 and made the Banate of Jajce

successors.name: Duchy of Saint Sava
successors.text: Hum, which Stjepan Vukcic Kosaca ruled as 'Herceg of Saint Sava' from 1448/49

ledger.x: 1377: Tvrtko I is crowned King of Bosnia at Mile.
1385: the Hungarian queens recognise Tvrtko's possession of Kotor (spring); he had built a fortress in the Bay of Kotor in early 1382 (the later Novi).
1390: the Dalmatian cities and islands surrender to Tvrtko, who styles himself 'king of Rascia, Bosnia, Dalmatia, Croatia, and Pomorje'.
1391: bridging entry, page silent on when Tvrtko's Dalmatian and Kotor acquisitions ended.
1399: Ragusa acquires the coast between the city and Pelješac.
1403: Bosnia and Ragusa go to war.
1404: the war ends with the Bosnian withdrawal; Ragusa keeps the strip.
1419: Sandalj Hranic sells eastern Konavle to Ragusa.
1426: Ragusa buys the rest of Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod, from Radoslav Pavlovic.
1448: Stjepan Vukcic becomes 'Herceg of Saint Sava' and Hum leaves the kingdom's drawn shape.
1463: Mehmed II conquers Bosnia and has King Stephen Tomasevic beheaded on 25 May.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Bosnia
wars.outcome: The Ottomans raided eastern Bosnia from 1384 and attacked the kingdom from about 1386; the conquest ended in May 1463 with the execution of Stephen Tomasevic.

wars.name: Ragusan-Bosnian war of 1403-1404
wars.outcome: 'ended with Bosnian withdrawal'; Ragusa kept the area it acquired in 1399.

wars.name: Hungarian-Bosnian conflict of 1404
wars.outcome: 'in June 1404, Tvrtko's supporters defeated a Hungarian army and thus prevented Ostoja from reclaiming the crown'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Siege of Jajce (1463)
wars.outcome: Jajce 'was captured by Hungarians under Matthias on 26 December 1463' and became the Banate of Jajce, which resisted until 1527.

certainty.note: Medieval Bosnia's frontiers are approximate throughout; the Ragusan frontier is the exception once Konavle was bought (1419 and 1426), but it is outside the kingdom's drawn shape.
